releases.name: ARMSX3 1.7.2
releases.body: # ARMSX3 1.7.2 ## New - **ZeroFG frame generation:** (experimental) adds frames between the ones a game draws, x2, x3 or x4, up to your display's refresh rate. It's in Settings > Performance and in the in-game menu. Switch it on before starting a game, switched on during one, it starts after Apply & Restart. By @hy300leosquizz-ctrl (#331).

releases.name: ARMSX3 for iOS 0.0.4 beta
releases.body:
## Graphics and memory

**Faster frame submission.** MoltenVK now turns each frame into Metal work on its own thread instead of on the graphics thread, so the graphics thread spends almost no time submitting a frame. Framebuffers are now freed only after the GPU has finished with them, which this needed. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Freed textures give their memory back.** Large texture allocations now get memory of their own, which goes back to iOS when the texture is freed. Before, one texture still in use kept a whole 64 MB block, and One Piece held 2.3 GB of blocks for 643 MB of textures. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Upload buffer space comes back sooner.** The texture upload buffer gives back finished space after every full GPU wait, where it held it until the next frame and swapped in a new buffer instead.

**No stall on the first new shader.** The shader compiler's one-time setup now happens at boot. It used to land in gameplay, on the first shader a game hadn't shown before. Thanks to RewindBox, whose work led to this.

**Black Ops II weapon.** The weapon in your hands no longer draws with its triangles over each other.

releases.name: ARMSX3 1.7.1
releases.body: # ARMSX3 1.7.1 ## Games - **Uncharted 2: Among Thieves, Super Street Fighter IV, Journey, and other games:** fixed the stop with "Failed to compile fragment shader" at the default Shader Precision (Low). - **Ratchet & Clank: Tools of Destruction:** fixed the freeze on Cobalia (thanks Seeslo for testing). -**Uncharted 3: Drake’s Deception** gets The Last of Us fix for freezes during play, since both games run the same job system, prevents freezes in UC3. ## Save states - **Save states from 1.7 and earlier don't load in 1.7.1,** because RPCS3's font module update changed the save state format. In-game saves are not affected.

releases.name: ARMSX3 1.7
releases.body: # ARMSX3 1.7 ## Highlights - **New SPU code compiles in the background.** Games keep running while it compiles, so new areas load without pausing. Games that need the old pause keep it. - **Compiled SPU code now carries over between updates,** including game updates, so first boots after them are quick. Each game compiles once more on its first boot after this update. ## The Last of Us - **Fixed the freeze during play.** The game hands its work to background jobs and waits for them, and on phones a job list could stop with work still in it, freezing the game anywhere from minutes to hours in. ARMSX3 now keeps those jobs moving.

releases.name: FF7Recomp 1.1.63
releases.body:
**Fixed: party names and mini avatars gone with Battle+, and the battle help text gone after Tifa's or Cait Sith's reels, with Enhanced Stock UI (#93)**

Reported in issue #93, both with Enhanced Stock UI:

**Names and mini avatars disappeared when Battle+ was on.** Enhanced Stock UI's mini avatars borrow one byte of each character's saved data during a battle: the byte right before the name, which normally holds the Limit gauge. It puts the avatar there and draws the name from that byte, so the avatar shows up in front of the name. Battle+ kept that byte full (255) in battle too. In FF7's text, 255 means "end of text", so the name and the avatar were both empty. Battle+ now fills that saved gauge only outside battle. In battle it fills the battle's own gauge, as before, so Limits are still ready every turn.

releases.name: FF7Recomp 1.1.62
releases.body:
**Fixed: crashes in some scenes with Echo-S voices and ChaOS's Resized Models (#91)**

Reported in issue #91: with Echo-S 7's voices on, the game closed in some scenes, for example on boarding the Highwind from the world map.

Two mods were each changing half of the same scene. ChaOS's **BETA: Resized Models** option replaces the list of character models for 693 scenes, a list made to match the original game's scene scripts. Echo-S's voiced version brings its own scene scripts, and in 39 scenes those use more characters than ChaOS's list loads. In the Highwind's deck, for example, the scripts use 14 models and ChaOS's list has 10. The game then tried to animate a character that was never loaded and crashed on the first frame. (ChaOS's own description of the option warns that it can crash with gameplay mods.)

Now, when a mod's model list doesn't match the models the scene's scripts use, that list is left out for that scene, and the scene keeps the models that came with its own file. In those 39 scenes the characters have their normal size instead of ChaOS's resized one; everywhere else Resized Models works as before. The log (`ff7.log`) names each scene where this happens.

releases.name: v1.1.61
releases.body:
**Fixed: rare crashes at scene changes with sound-effect mods on (#90)**

Reported in issue #90: once in a while the game closed when entering a battle, leaving the menu, or moving between areas, more often with many mods on and little free memory. The crash records all showed the same thing: some other part of the app had a pointer whose lower half had been overwritten with zeros earlier on.

We tracked it down with a special memory-checking build on our test device, which caught it within a minute. The cause was in FFNx's sound-effect code, which is active whenever a mod replaces the game's sound effects (Echo-S, the Tsunamods set and others). It keeps one record per sound channel. Some calls used the wrong channel number, and every battle transition touched a channel that had no record. Each time, the game wrote a few bytes just past the end of that table, usually zeros, into memory that belonged to something else. Most of the time nothing happened; sometimes it hit a pointer, and whatever used that pointer next crashed.

releases.name: v1.1.60
releases.body:
**Fixed: the game could close a while after loading a save state from an earlier session (#91)**

Reported in issue #91 with Echo-S 7 voices on. The game keeps one data file open the whole time it runs: the sound archive it loads its own sound effects from. A save state stores the game's memory, and that memory held the open file's handle as it was in the session where the state was made. After you closed the game and loaded the state in a later session, that handle no longer pointed at anything. The next time a scene needed a sound the game hadn't loaded yet, the game crashed.

Whether you hit this depended on luck. It was more likely with mods that open many files, like Echo-S voices.

Save states now record which files the game has open, and opening them again is part of loading a state. States made with older versions are covered too: the sound archive is opened again when they load.

### Updating
Go to **Settings → Updates** in the launcher (or install this APK over your current version), then press **Play**. It asks to **Update the game** once (a few seconds).

APK SHA-256: `f29167fd9f2e8d88814386aacf28742669a42cc58810be4dca13f5972d3dd3ab`

releases.name: v1.1.59
releases.body:
**New: the launcher says what kind of device runs the game best, and what helps after a crash**

Suggested in issue #90. Rare crashes when a battle or scene is drawn for the first time are most often the phone running low on memory while the graphics driver prepares that scene's shaders. That is a hardware limit more than a bug, so the launcher now says so where you'll see it:

- **After the game crashes** (or Android closes it for memory), the launcher shows a short note once: what most often causes it, what helps, and a button to **Report a problem** if it keeps happening.
- **Report a problem** and **Game files** (first setup) show the recommendation.
- **Settings → Renderer** now recommends **OpenGL ES** on Mali GPUs (most MediaTek and Exynos phones).
- The README has the same line under *Playing*.

The recommendation: **8 GB of RAM or more, with other apps (browser tabs too) closed while you play.** Heavy mod sets need the most memory, above all on Vulkan. On Mali GPUs, OpenGL ES is usually the steadier choice.

![The note the launcher shows once after the game crashed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bhuiyah/ff7-recomp-android/main/docs/release-images/1.1.59-crash-tip.jpg)

releases.body:
You need **Xbox360 Call of Duty 3 (USA, Europe).iso** file for install!

> **Still in development: bugs can and will occur.**
> *Még fejlesztés alatt: hibák előfordulhatnak.*

The first release since [0.4.0](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.4.0): one executable that keeps itself up to date, the game's own menus played with the mouse, prompts that name your keys, and a faster renderer.

## New

- **One file: `CoD3SP_s.exe`.** FFmpeg's libraries for the sound and the films are built into it; nothing else to unpack.
- **Updates itself.** At every start it asks GitHub for a newer release; if there is one, it downloads it, replaces itself and starts the new version. Turn it off with `auto_update = 0` under `[game]` in `CoD3Recomp.ini`, or start it with `--no-update`.
- **New first start.** The console window asks whether this is a fresh install (choose your disc image, then the folder to install into) or the game is already installed (choose the game's main folder, the one with `default.xex`).

releases.name: Call of Duty 3 - PC Port - 0.4.0
releases.body:
You need **Xbox360 Call of Duty 3 (USA, Europe).iso** file for install!

> **Still in development: bugs can and will occur.**
> *Még fejlesztés alatt: hibák előfordulhatnak.*

The first release since [0.3.0](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.3.0): a faster game, a picture closer to the console's, and two experimental options that make it faster still.

## New

- **Faster on every level.** The emulated kernel woke every waiting thread whenever anything was signalled (one of the game's locks is released some 50,000 times a second); now only the threads waiting for that object wake. The game's CPU use dropped from about 5.4 cores to 3.3, and the forest at 1080p without MSAA went from about 91 to 95–108 frames a second.
- **Native command lists (experimental)**, in the F11 menu, after a restart. The draws are made from the game's own Direct3D calls, and the console's GPU command stream is run only for what the GPU still has to do. With **Watch memory writes (experimental)** also on, the forest at 1080p without MSAA runs at about 180 frames a second. Tested on eight levels, the films and mission restarts; off by default until it has been played more.

## New

- **The next mission after a win.** The console restarts the game between missions and hands the next one over; the port does the same, so a finished mission leads into the next one instead of closing the game.
- **A mission's briefing film can be skipped** with Space (A) once its level has loaded. On the console it always plays to its end.
- **Unlimited frame rate in levels** (settings menu, on by default). A level runs at what the machine can do, around 100 to 115 frames a second where it had 60; the menus stay at 60 and the films at their own 30. The game's speed does not change with the frame rate.

releases.name: Call of Duty 3 - PC Port - 0.2.3
releases.body:
You need **Xbox360 Call of Duty 3 (USA, Europe).iso** file for install!

A fix release over [0.2.2](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.2), and the one worth updating for: the lighting is right now.

## Fixed

**Walls lit far too brightly, and the odd shading on the soldiers and on the player's hands.** An instruction of the console's shaders has a vector half and a scalar half, and they run together: both read the registers as they were before the instruction and only then write. The translation wrote the vector's result first, so a scalar that read the very register the vector wrote got the new value instead of the old one.

The game's third light per surface is written exactly that way. Its scalar wants the specular exponent times a logarithm; with the write first it took a dot product instead, and two to the tenth of that became the specular. Every lit stone wall in Mayenne came out white with pink and green speckle, and characters were shaded oddly for the same reason. Eighty of the six hundred shader programs a level draws with have such an instruction, so this shows up all over the game, not only on that wall.

## Known issues

releases.name: Call of Duty 3 - PC Port - 0.2.2
releases.body:
You need **Xbox360 Call of Duty 3 (USA, Europe).iso** file for install!

A fix release over [0.2.1](https://github.com/FrankHUN88453/CoD3Recomp/releases/tag/v0.2.1); everything below is on top of what 0.2.1 brought.

## Fixed

**The HUD and the menu still flickered.** 0.2.1 looked at every texture every frame again, but a large one that had been still for a while was only *sampled*: sixty four places out of it. The HUD's fonts, icons and compass are small and change a handful of texels at a time, and the samples missed those changes, so the old picture stayed up for a frame. Everything up to two megabytes is now hashed whole, every frame, and only what is bigger than that falls back to sampling.

**Shadow filtering collapsed.** A texture fetch on the console carries three signed offsets in halves of a texel. The game's shadows are one map fetched four times at the corners of a texel; with the offsets dropped those were four fetches of the same texel, so a surface came out wholly lit or wholly dark instead of softly edged.

releases.body:
# v0.0.8.2 Experimental — Stability Update & On-Screen Control Editor

Small stability update on top of `v0.0.7.9-experimental`. Still experimental — please use **EXPORT LOGS** when reporting anything.

## New: customize the on-screen controls

A **CUSTOMIZE** pill now sits next to **TOUCH** in the HUD. It opens an in-place editor:

- Tap a control to select it, then **drag** to move it.
- **S- / S+** resize, **O- / O+** change opacity.
- **BIND** cycles a button's guest input index.
- **PRESET** cycles DEFAULT → COMPACT → LEFT → RIGHT.
- **RESET** restores the original layout, **DONE** saves and exits.

Layouts are stored as normalized coordinates, so they survive rotation/window resizing and app restarts. Guest input is suppressed while the editor is open (no phantom presses), gamepad focus rules are unchanged, and **TOUCH: OFF** also leaves edit mode.

## Stability / rendering correctness (from the in-progress post-0.0.7.9 patch)

- Pixel shaders now use full FP32 with NaN-safe multiply helpers (`mulL`/`mulL1`), clamp-before-scale texture adjustment, and `isnan()` output sanitization — removes FP16 overflow/NaN artifacts without changing the guest shader set.

## BioShock 1 Native Android ReComp — v0.0.7.9 Experimental

### Highlights & Fixes

- **Fixed Missing Initial Lighting / Pitch-Black Areas on Boot (No Longer Requires Tapping `RES`)**
  - Fixed Xenos `DI_PT_RECTLIST` clear redirection in `PrimaryColorTargetAt()` / `PrimaryDepthTargetAt()` so direct `msaa=0` clears are never stolen by wider targets sharing the same EDRAM base (`0x5a0` / `0x5b0`), and 4x-MSAA fast-clear aliases (`msaa=2`) only redirect to exact `pitch * 2` non-MSAA targets (`640→1280`, `280→560`, `80→160`).

  - Initialized newly allocated `GL_DEPTH24_STENCIL8` depth targets and resolved depth surfaces to `1.0` (`ClearDepthTextureOne`) so fresh targets never read `0.0` or recycled VRAM garbage across boot, level loads, or live resolution switches.
  - Armed physical write watches on resolved surfaces, added periodic eviction of dead menu/loading-screen resolved targets (300+ idle frames), and rejected compressed DXT/BC texture fetches from matching stale resolved targets.

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.1.0 (beta)
releases.body:
CapyPS5 0.1.0 is the **first beta**: faster on every game, fewer crashes, and on-screen controls you can lay out yourself. PS4 backward compatibility stays experimental. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**Faster**
- **The GPU thread runs on the fastest CPU cores.** On a Snapdragon 8 Elite this alone made a demanding Unreal Engine 4 level about a third faster.
- **Less waiting for the GPU.** Several cases where the emulator stopped to read back data the GPU had just written are gone:
  - fast-clear metadata fills now run on the CPU;
  - GPU-driven draws of PS4 games are executed on the GPU;
  - fresh buffer data is copied without a system call per page.
  The same level gained about 30 % more on top.
- **Cheaper per-draw work:** shader resource tables are read in one go per table on ARM, which halved the cost of preparing each draw.

**More stable**
- Unreal Engine games that closed with a corrupt memory error a few seconds into a level (the game's own allocator reporting a broken "canary", or a crash reading address 1) no longer do: the emulator stopped waiting for a GPU signal that was only late.

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.6
releases.body:
Sixth alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android, and the first with **PS4 backward compatibility**: PS4 games now run in CapyPS5 the way they do on a real PS5. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**New: PS4 backward compatibility**

A PS5 runs PS4 games on its own hardware. CapyPS5 does the same in software: PS4 games use the same x86-64 JIT, system libraries and Vulkan renderer as PS5 games, and only what the PS4 does differently was added.
- **GPU:** PS4 (GCN gfx7) shaders and registers, PS4 render targets and texture tiling, CMASK and HTile fast clears, cube and volume textures, and the PS4 Gnm driver calls.
- **System:** PS4 executables and the modules games ship, the PS4 memory layout and flexible memory budget, and PS4 save data and trophies.
- PS4 games go in the same game folders as PS5 games (a folder with `eboot.bin` and `sce_sys/param.sfo`) and carry a **PS4** mark in the library.
- This is the first release with it. 2D and Unity games run best; Unreal Engine 4 games start but are slow; many games don't boot yet. Lower the resolution for big games.

**Also new**

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.5
releases.body:
Fifth alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android. Mali GPUs on their system driver can now run games, and the FPS counter shows how many frames CapyPS5 Framegen adds. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**New**
- **Mali on the system driver:** that driver cannot sample BCn compressed textures, so the GPU used to be rejected. CapyPS5 now decompresses those textures on the GPU when it uploads them (BC1 to BC7, including BC6H HDR textures). GPUs that support BCn keep using it directly.
- **PanVK on Mali:** the GPU is no longer rejected when the driver lacks vertex-stage stores or dual-source blending.
- **Framegen counter:** with CapyPS5 Framegen on, the FPS counter reads *XX FPS - YY FG*: XX are the game's own frames, YY the total including generated ones. The options are now called *Framegen x2*, *x3* and *x4*.
- **HDR10 output:** games that output HDR10 are converted to SDR for the screen.

**Fixed**
- Tessellation: quad domains, fractional-even spacing, counterclockwise output and masked hull control points.

releases.name: CapyPS5 v0.0.4
releases.body:
Fourth alpha of the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android. More than 100 games now run correctly according to testers' reports, and this release adds CapyPS5 Framegen. Existing installs are offered this update in the app.

**New**
- **CapyPS5 Framegen:** optional frame generation. It draws in-between frames from the motion between two game frames, so a game at 30 FPS is shown at 60. Off by default; turn it on in *Settings → Performance* (1 per frame, or up to 3). Adds one frame of latency and some GPU load; works best from 25 FPS up.
- New performance options in *Settings → Performance*: shadow resolution, early depth testing and a frame rate limit (30 or 20 FPS).
- Physical keyboard input and an on-screen keyboard toggle for text fields, and system dialogs that can now be answered.
- Android 16 and devices with 16 KB memory pages are supported.

**Fixed**
- Unreal Engine 5 games: graphics and async compute hand work back and forth several times per frame, and each hand-off waited up to 100 ms. Menus that ran at 0–2 FPS now move.
- Games whose shadows use depth-compare texture gathers (Castlevania: Belmont's Curse) closed after the menu.

releases.body:
## No more blinking objects after loading

While the game is running, each new combination of shader and render state needs a GPU pipeline. Pipelines the app has never seen are built in the background so the game doesn't freeze, and until one is ready the objects that use it are not drawn. Until now that also happened to pipelines it had already built in an earlier session. releases.name: v1.2.6: save backups, movies keep their shape, every controller works
releases.body:
**Save backups, movies that keep their shape, and two controllers at once.**

- **Save backups** (*CTRL → Game → Save backups …*): copies of all your save slots in a folder you choose, outside the app, so uninstalling the game doesn't delete them. A copy is made after the game saves, at most every 10 minutes. The latest 10 and one for each of the last 7 days played are kept, up to 64 MB in all (the latest 3 always). A backup can be restored from the same screen; it takes effect at the next start, and the saves it replaces are kept aside.
- **Movies are never stretched.** They keep their 16:9 shape with **Wide screen** on, and now also with **Stretch to fill wide screens** on. A movie whose own picture has black bars at the top and bottom as well (bars on all four sides) is zoomed in, centred, until one pair of bars is gone, without cutting anything off.
- **Controllers:** every connected controller now controls the game. Before, with two connected (for example a handheld's built-in controls and an external pad), the second one's buttons were ignored.

releases.name: v1.2.5: render resolution and true wide screens
releases.body:
**Choose the render resolution, and true wide screens.**

- **Resolution** (*CTRL → Image*, applies at the next start): **540p**, **720p** (as on the Xbox 360, the default) or **1080p**. The 3D world is drawn at that size; menus and the HUD stay sharp at 720p. 540p is faster and a little softer. 1080p is scaled down into the 720p picture, which smooths edges rather than adding detail, and needs a fast GPU.
- **Wide screen** (*CTRL → Image*, applies at the next start): on screens wider than 16:9 (most phones), the 3D world fills the whole screen, with more to see at the sides instead of black bars or stretching. Menus, the HUD and the minimap stay in the middle, laid out as on a 16:9 screen, and movies keep 16:9 with black bars. It costs some speed: on a Galaxy S10 (Adreno 640) the field runs at about 24.5 fps instead of 28. Off by default.
- With both left at their defaults, the picture is the same as in v1.2.4.

releases.name: v1.2.4: tidier CTRL menu with Exit game, fixes for more phones
releases.body:
**A tidier CTRL menu with Exit game, and fixes for more phones from the Dark Souls II port.**

- **CTRL menu:** the options are now in sections that open one at a time: *Controls*, *Frame rate and performance*, *Image*, *Second screen*, *Game* and *Troubleshooting*. **Exit game** (top right) closes the game after asking; save in the game's main menu first. After changing an option marked *, the menu offers to restart the game so it takes effect.
- **CTRL button:** under *Controls* it can stay on screen, slide into a small tab when not in use, or go away 30 seconds after the game starts. Once it's gone, Android's Back button or gesture opens the menu.
- **Frame rate:** one list with 30, 40, 60 and *60 fps, smoother* (the former 120 Hz option).
- **Mali GPUs (Dimensity, Exynos, Tensor):** the app now starts on Arm's own driver, with the renderer settings that fixed Mali players' glitches in the Dark Souls II port, which shares this renderer. Still untested on a real Mali phone: reports with logs are welcome.
- **Adreno 8xx (Snapdragon 8 Elite):** Turnip now runs in sysmem mode there, which fixed GPU hangs on these chips in the Dark Souls II port.

releases.name: v1.2.3: fix for Adreno 600-series GPUs
releases.body:
**Fix for Adreno 600-series GPUs (Snapdragon 855 / 865 / 870 / 888 and similar).**

- **Adreno 6xx:** the renderer no longer loses work on these GPUs. Missing menu text, garbled or black pictures and wrong colours came from the Turnip driver on Adreno 6xx dropping some of the renderer's compute work (texture loads and render-to-texture copies) when it was set up while a drawing pass was still open. The fix closes the pass first. It was found by the Dark Souls II port's frame capture on an Adreno 640 and tested here on a Galaxy S10 (Adreno 640) (#4). Adreno 7xx/8xx draw the same as before, at the same speed.

**Updating from v1.2.2:** install `lr-recomp-android-arm64.apk` (below) over it. Your saves, game files, shaders and settings are kept.

releases.name: v1.2.2: infinite HP, stretch to fill wide screens
releases.body:
**Infinite HP, and a stretch option for wide phone screens.**

- **Infinite HP (in battle):** a new cheat under **CTRL → Cheats**. Lightning's HP goes back to its maximum after every hit. A single hit larger than her maximum HP can still knock her out (#5).
- **Infinite EP** checked in battle, including the first tutorial battle: Overclock and the other EP abilities are refilled at once (#5).
- **Stretch to fill wide screens:** a new option under **CTRL → Image**. On phones wider than 16:9 it removes the black bars at the sides by stretching the picture sideways. It applies the next time the game starts (#6).
- **Regression tests:** a battle test for both cheats on the Thor.

**Updating from v1.2.1:** install `lr-recomp-android-arm64.apk` (below) over it. Your saves, game files, shaders and settings are kept.

Fixes the ConsolePort wizard reappearing on every login ([reported on Reddit](https://www.reddit.com/r/EmulationOnAndroid/)).

If you interacted with the addon's controller-setup wizard during your very first login, WoW saved a half-finished configuration that blocked the automatic setup from ever applying — so the wizard kept coming back. The app now re-checks your account every time you press PLAY and repairs that state automatically (your previous file is kept as `ConsolePort.lua.bak`).

**If you were affected:** update, exit the game completely, press PLAY again. The wizard should be gone and the full pad mapped.

Also clarifies the first-login instructions shown in the app. Non-English clients (frFR, deDE, …) are fully supported — the locale was unrelated to this bug.

releases.name: WoW Mobile v0.1.1
releases.body:
First public release.

**WoW Mobile** runs World of Warcraft 3.3.5a (Wrath of the Lich King) on Android with touch controls designed for [ConsolePortLK](https://github.com/leoaviana/ConsolePortLK). It is a single-purpose fork of [Winlator](https://github.com/brunodev85/winlator) (LGPL-2.1).

## Install
1. Download and sideload `wow-mobile-v0.1.1.apk` (installs alongside stock Winlator — separate app id `it.wowmobile`)
2. Put your own WoW 3.3.5a (build 12340) client folder on the phone's storage — **no game files are included**
3. Open the app → allow storage → *Select game folder* → PLAY

On first launch the app installs the bundled ConsolePortLK addons, calibrates the bindings, sets the realmlist (changeable in WoW Settings) and creates a tuned Wine container. After your first login, log out once so it can finish per-account calibration — then everything just works.

## Highlights
- One-tap play: folder validation, addon install, key bindings, realmlist and graphics config are all automatic and idempotent — an already-configured folder is never damaged

releases.body:
**Console Five Pro v0.0.9proQ4** — an independent rebranded build of CapyPS5 v0.0.3, the first PlayStation 5 emulator for Android (built on KytyPS5 and the FEX x86-64 JIT).

## v0.0.9proQ4 — the freeze fix, the after-freeze crash, frame flow in heavy 3D (same graphics)
- **Fixed: the multi-second freezes.** A draw whose pipeline was still compiling used to block the renderer with an *unbounded* wait on the compile queue. A storm of first-visit pipelines (a new area, material streaming, one-shot LUT passes) could then park the whole renderer behind the workers for tens of seconds - the field logs show 14-28 s of frozen video and starved audio right before the session died. No draw waits more than `debug.capy.pipeline_wait_ms` (default 4 ms, 0 = never wait) now: past the bound the draw is skipped, the compile lands in the background, and the next occurrence draws for real. Every pipeline miss is queued to the async workers - the renderer never compiles inline during play.

releases.name: The Sims 2 for Android 0.3.1-dev
releases.body:
The Sims 2 for Android **0.3.1-dev** improves Lua error handling, material creation, renderer diagnostics, texture conversion, and the launcher. Changes since **0.3-dev**, from signed source commit `a84f6585caca7a90afe140540714f879800c33bb`.

One APK includes **arm64-v8a** and experimental **armeabi-v7a**. The minimum requirements are now **Android 8.0 (API 26)** and **OpenGL ES 3.1**; the native Vulkan renderer accepts **Vulkan 1.0**. Game data must come from a compatible The Sims 2 Legacy Collection installation. Android 8.0–8.1 and GLES 3.1-only devices still need further device testing.

## Stability and startup

- Fixed the embedded MSVC `setjmp/longjmp` implementation used by Lua: returning to an error handler now unwinds the actual native call stack as well as restoring guest state. The bridge covers all 34 original setjmp call sites and both longjmp epilogues.
- Handle nested and repeated Lua errors, restore exception state, and remove jump contexts when their function returns, a C++ handler unwinds past them, or their thread ends. A jump to a function that has already returned is diagnosed.

releases.name: The Sims 2 for Android 0.3-dev
releases.body:
One APK now supports both **arm64-v8a** and experimental **armeabi-v7a**. The port requires Android 10 or later, OpenGL ES 3.2, and game data from a compatible The Sims 2 Legacy Collection installation. ARM32 also requires Thumb-2, NEON, and 4 KiB kernel pages. Android chooses the ABI, and the app unpacks the matching XZ-compressed engine on first use.

## Graphics and performance

- Fixed flickering and missing objects on Mali-G51 in OpenGL ES. The workaround defaults to on and can be changed in Advanced renderer settings. Fixed a related driver hang reproduced on Mali-T830.
- OpenGL ES compiles and links uncached shader programs in the background, reducing stalls when zooming out, rotating the camera, or changing floors.
- The in-game **Minimal Graphics** preset lowers 11 settings to reduce memory use. It saves the previous values, persists across restarts, and restores those values when switched off.
- **Android performance hints (ADPF) are off by default.** The launcher still lets you turn them on for the next game start.

releases.name: The Sims 2 for Android 0.2.1-dev

## What's new since 0.2-dev

- **Vulkan textures.** DXT1, DXT3, and DXT5 now use the correct BC formats on drivers that support them. This fixes colored noise on terrain, roads, and trees seen on Adreno 735 with both the system Vulkan driver and Turnip.
- **OpenGL ES.** Fixed dynamic buffer updates that could corrupt neighborhood chooser panels and text on Adreno 650 and 735, and the neighborhood HUD on Adreno 650.
- **Vulkan UI scaling.** The APK now includes precompiled SPIR-V variants for FSR 1 UI scaling for all 81 pixel shader entries and the built-in fixed-function pixel shader. Shaders outside the library, including shaders used by some mods, can still be compiled on the device.
- **Shader coverage.** The bundled library grew from 194 to 380 captured shaders and from 215 to 408 entries, including sampler variants. The updated capture tool checks bytecode hashes and records sampler variants. A strict diagnostic mode and a library format check help verify coverage.

## Install or update

Download the APK below or check for updates in the launcher. This build supports ARM64 devices running Android 10 or later and requires compatible The Sims 2 Legacy Collection game files.

releases.body:
Development release for the Android ARM64 port of The Sims 2 Legacy Collection. The supported PC source is Steam build 18015495. See the [build and installation guide](https://github.com/phys-winner/pc_decomp_ts2/blob/f2b7cce5/readme.md) for requirements and instructions.

### Graphics and diagnostics

- OpenGL ES is now the default renderer. An explicitly selected renderer takes priority when it is available.
- Added DXVK with Mesa PanVK for compatible ARM Mali and Immortalis GPUs. The launcher checks the active driver and its Vulkan 1.3 capabilities, and supports importing a custom PanVK driver. The bundled kbase driver requires 4 KiB kernel pages. On Redmi Note 8 Pro (begonia) and TB373FU, PanVK uses linear buffers to address frame corruption.
- Added a live FPS counter and frame-time graph across renderers. The extended view shows system, GPU, memory, battery, thermal, and display information where Android makes it available.
- Improved Android surface handling in OpenGL ES and DXVK, including EGL recovery after a failed window bind. Added validation for shader bytecode, D3DX constant tables, GLSL generation, and texture dimensions and row pitches.

releases.name: Version 5.10.2
releases.body:
Changes:

- Fix authentication for registries without token service: Nexus, Artifactory and htpasswd-protected servers.
- Report bad `PD_DOCKER_AUTH` credentials before initiating install or push session.

releases.name: Version 5.10.1
releases.body:
Changes:

* `install`, `push`: better handling for registry rate limits (HTTP 429) by honoring `Retry-After`, show detailed error when rate limit occurs while using a shared Docker Hub frontend (proxy) instead of raw `Network error: HTTP Error 429`.

Notice for users: this does not resolve issue with rate limits imposed by Docker Hub registry. Such issue just can't be resolved at proot-distro side because restriction applies to client IP address, which in case of NAT (CG-NAT) or proxy may be shared between large amount of devices.

Don't submit bug reports if encounter HTTP 429!

Workaround:

1. Create Docker Hub account.
2. Use `export PD_DOCKER_AUTH="username:password"` or `export PD_DOCKER_AUTH="username:personal-access-token"`, the personal access token must be created through account settings with permissions at least for read-only access.

releases.name: Version 5.10.0
releases.body:
Changes:

- refs: Image names are now checked using Docker's rules. Malformed names are refused with a clear message.
- install: Added support for images pinned by digest, e.g. `ubuntu@sha256:...`. The download is verified against the digest. A pinned image can be reinstalled from the cache without network.
- build, push: A digest is refused in `build -t` and `push`.
- install: Fixed intact image layers sometimes refused with "does not match its digest".
- http: Redirects can no longer move a download from HTTPS to plain HTTP. `--allow-insecure` lifts this.
- registry: `--allow-insecure` no longer applies to Docker Hub. It is always verified.
- http: Network requests give up after 2 minutes of silence instead of hanging forever.
- http: Invalid URLs and registry addresses now show an error message instead of a traceback.
- build, login: Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 in arguments, build args or image environment no longer cause a traceback.
- list, remove: `--image` no longer prints control characters from cache entries as they are.
- sync, copy: Files that change during the transfer are handled correctly. No more missed updates or wrong permissions.

releases.name: Version 5.9.0
releases.body:
Changes:

- `login`, `run`: export variables `PD_CONTAINER=<name>`, `PD_IMAGE=<image-ref>`, `PD_IMAGE_ID=<sha256-digest>` and `container=proot-distro` in sessions. Build gets same except `PD_CONTAINER`.
- `pull`: detect whether image config or manifest is shorter than `Content-Length`.
- `build` (ADD, COPY): placing directory over an existing regular file is now a refusal instead of a silent tree/layer mismatch.
- `build` (... --chmod): validate value as an octal between 0 and 07777.
- `build`: Dockerfile is read with 16 MiB limit.
- `push`: send the Bearer token on the upload PUT only when the Location URL belongs to the registry itself.
- Registry credentials are only sent to the origin they were addressed to.
- Do not carry Authorization header if host redirects from HTTPS to HTTP.
- A token endpoint realm must be `https://` (`http://` allowed under --allow-insecure). `file://`, `ftp://` and `data:` realms are refused.
- Environment strings from image config are validated before exec (no NUL, encodable, under 128 KiB).
- The `profile.d` snippet is written for every session of a normal-type container, not only default-mode Termux logins.

# Oblivion for Android 0.1.3

APK: `Oblivion-0.1.3.apk` (arm64-v8a, Android 9+, Vulkan 1.1).
SHA-1 `e74c55c378825480eedb6b2c781946bc4bef3555`

## Fixed
- Mali GPUs: geometry no longer explodes into streaks on Mali GPUs (Exynos, Dimensity, Tensor, Kirin), which lack the clip-distance feature.

## Performance
- Each thread keeps its own cache of recently freed small blocks and reuses them without taking the global heap lock. In testing, an allocate-and-free went from about 34 ms to 5 ms. Freeing the same block twice is still detected and logged though.
- A thread that re-enters a lock it already holds now just counts up the way Windows does, instead of going through the real lock each time.
- Memory copies: the base memcpy routine, about 10% of all CPU, now runs as Android's native copy.
- The game reads the clock hundreds of thousands of times a second. QueryPerformanceCounter, GetTickCount and timeGetTime now read the processor's hardware timer instead of making a system call.
- A missing Data folder is now remembered after the first check - no repeated path search and log line each time.

Please attach `port/log.txt` from your Oblivion folder to any bug report.

releases.name: v1.0.0 — Winlator 适配包
releases.body:
在 Android（[Winlator](https://github.com/brunodev85/winlator)）与 ARM Linux（Wine + Box64）上运行 DFLegacy 60 版单机端的适配包。

## 包含

| 文件 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `d3d8.dll` | d3d8to9 v1.15.1 预编译包装层（x86，124 KB） |
| `LICENSE.md` | d3d8to9 的 BSD-3-Clause 许可 |
| `使用说明.md` | 完整部署说明 |
| `放置说明.txt` | 快速上手 |

## 解决什么问题

客户端是 2008 年的 32 位程序，**只认 Direct3D 8**。Android 上的 DXVK 只支持 D3D9 及以上，直接跑会黑屏或崩溃。

这个 `d3d8.dll` 把 D3D8 调用逐条翻译成 D3D9：

```
DNF.exe → d3d8.dll → D3D9 → DXVK → Vulkan → Adreno / Mali
```

绕开 Wine 自带的 `wined3d → OpenGL` 路径，走 Vulkan 后端。

## 用法

1. 解压，把 `d3d8.dll` 复制到 `DNF.exe` 同级目录
2. Winlator 容器里设 `WINEDLLOVERRIDES=d3d8=n,b`
3. Box86 / Box64 都打开，DXVK 选 2.x
4. 运行 `DNF.exe`

**Windows 本机不要放这个文件** —— 原生 D3D8 路径工作正常，放进去反而改变渲染路径。

## 前提

服务端需要是 x86 构建（NativeAOT `-r win-x86`），否则在纯 32 位环境里加载不了。相关改动见 [DFLegacyAot](https://github.com/Yoshino-Loli/DFLegacyAot)。

## 未验证项

- `ijl15.dll` 的 WIC JPEG 解码在 Wine 下的表现
- Job Object 的退出联动在 Wine 下的可靠性（失败时手动结束服务端即可）

真机帧数需自行测试，骁龙 8 系预期 25~40 fps。

## 不包含

游戏客户端本体与任何受版权保护的资源。`DNF.exe`、`Script.pvf`、`ImagePacks2` 等权利归原权利人所有。

releases.body:
## ZeraPS5 v0.1.1-b1215

This Windows x64 release builds on b1214 and includes two graphics fixes and one CPU compatibility fix.

- Refresh tightly packed, single-channel texture atlases after small updates so letters remain visible in menus.
- Preserve the alpha channel when writing to the single-channel masks used by the GTA VI warning, Privacy Policy and Terms of Service panels.
- Emulate the PS5 CLZERO instruction when the host CPU raises an illegal-instruction exception. The instruction sequence reported on Intel passed an isolated test. An end-to-end retest on the affected Intel laptop is pending.

### Validation

- 196 automated checks passed on Windows, including 35 Vulkan checks on the RTX 5060 Ti.
- The b1214 installer applied the final ZIP in an isolated installation. Save, configuration, game and system-module test markers were preserved. Rollback and interrupted-installation recovery passed.
- The packaged executable displayed the Portuguese photosensitivity warning on the RTX 5060 Ti. An earlier development run of the same text fixes also displayed the Privacy Policy and Terms of Service and stopped with both boxes unchecked. Prologue gameplay remains unverified.

releases.name: ZeraPS5 v0.1.1-b1214 — Shader compiler update
releases.body:
## ZeraPS5 0.1.1 build 1214

This Windows x64 release updates the Vulkan shader compiler and includes the launcher and GPU writeback fixes shipped in b1192.

The translator simplifies a waterfall loop when it can prove that the emulated lane runs the body once. The new regression check covers both that case and a saved-mask register overlap where the loop must be retained.

Development testing of Grand Theft Auto VI reached the loading screen. The observation covers startup through loading. The translator change can trigger pipeline recreation on the first run.

### Validation

- 196 automated checks passed in the final serial runs, including 35 Vulkan checks on an RTX 5060 Ti.
- The b1192 updater installed the final ZIP in an isolated copy, preserved all five test data markers and passed rollback and interrupted-installation recovery.
- The Windows ZIP and the matching source archive were verified against the included checksums. Credits, component licenses and FFmpeg relink materials are included.

Use **Check for updates** in the launcher or download the Windows x64 ZIP below. Matching source and SHA-256 checksums are available on this page.
